protocol.description: An app tells the compositor how to present its window. With full-size content the compositor does not add its title bar above the content: the app draws its own toolbar (unified with the title bar) and the sidebar up to the top, and the compositor only draws the window buttons over the content, at the top left, vertically centered in the toolbar height.

description.summary: back to the normal appearance on the next commit

request.name: set_full_size_content
request.description: toolbar_height is the height, in logical pixels, of the toolbar the app draws at the top: the window buttons are vertically centered in that band. 0 goes back to the compositor's title bar. Values above 200 are clamped to 200.

description.summary: light or dark presentation of a window

request.name: set_appearance

description.summary: override the appearance of this window

request.description: Everything the compositor draws for the window follows the chosen appearance instead of the system's: the window buttons, the plain title bar and its title, the shadow and inner border, the glass regions declared by the window and the arrangement popover opened from its buttons. An app that is always dark (as on macOS, where NSWindow.appearance overrides the system's) asks for dark. system, the default, follows the system again. An unknown value is a protocol error (invalid_appearance). Double-buffered, applied on the next wl_surface.commit.

request.name: set_hidden

description.summary: hide or show the window without closing it

request.description: A non-zero hidden takes the window off the screen, out of the window lists and out of the focus, as if it were closed, but the app keeps its surface and its state: closing an app's last window does not end the app (silica-os/silica-desktop#142). Zero brings the window back where it was, focused; for a window that is already on screen it raises and focuses it (the app was opened again while the window sat behind others). Applied at once, not on the next commit.

request.name: set_size_increment
request.description: Interactive resizing snaps the content size (the surface's window geometry, in logical pixels) to base + n * step on each axis, with the nearest n that respects the minimum and maximum size. A terminal asks for its cell size (base: the padding). A step of 0 leaves that axis free; all steps 0 goes back to free resizing. Double-buffered, applied on the next wl_surface.commit.
